analysis.title: AI quick pulse: Funding the next three trillion in AI capex
key_insights: UBS raises its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 (from USD 900bn) and USD 1.4tr in 2027 (from USD 1.2tr), and introduces a USD 1.5tr forecast for 2028, citing stronger spending commitments from the largest hyperscalers and SpaceX.
The 2027 forecast implies AI capex growth of 38% to USD 1.4tr.

The funding mix is shifting. After four years in which hyperscaler cash flows funded much of the buildout, incremental investment increasingly draws on debt, equity, leases and supplier-backed financing.

Credit markets differentiate sharply between projects with and without strong hyperscaler or sponsor backing. CoreWeave's 2032 bond yielded around 15% in mid-October and its five-year CDS traded near 1,100bps, implying roughly a 60% five-year default probability under the assumed recovery rate.

UBS sees neocloud financing stress as a risk to the pace and composition of AI investment, not at this stage to the overall capex cycle. Selective project delays, repricing and consolidation are judged more likely than a broad collapse in spending.

The Big 4 US hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) plus SpaceX account for around 80% of the 2027 forecast, with assumed 10-year debt financing costs of 6-8%. Neoclouds account for only around 8%.

Vendor support is a funding channel: Broadcom's residual-value backstop for senior debt in a USD 63bn vehicle leasing its chips and networking equipment to Anthropic reduces residual-value risk, but deepens circular financial links among AI vendors, infrastructure providers and customers.

Equity markets are bridging the funding gap. Meta has USD 35bn of common-stock and mandatory-convertible-preferred offerings and a planned additional share-sale program of up to USD 60bn, for potential fundraising of USD 95bn. Alphabet priced an equity package in June 2026 with potential gross proceeds of around USD 85bn, including a USD 40bn at-the-market program that began in 3Q26.
Other major spenders could turn to equity as well, which shifts part of the investor debate from credit risk toward dilution and returns on incremental capital.

UBS flags a rising risk of a mid-cycle capex digestion over the next 12 months. Signposts: hyperscaler backlog conversion, AI-lab and cloud revenue growth, cloud and GPU hourly pricing, neocloud credit spreads and CDS, financing conditions, and project deferrals or renegotiations.

UBS would turn more cautious if falling AI costs fail to stimulate enough incremental usage to absorb capacity, or if algorithmic efficiency materially cuts compute needs while accelerator deployment and memory capacity keep growing, particularly in mainland China.

Strategy: a barbell of leading megacaps and defensive tech (payment networks, selected consumer-electronics companies hurt by rising memory costs) with high-quality AI picks and shovels that have durable demand, strong balance sheets and lower oversupply risk.

AI-related stocks have risen 2-3x over four years. UBS urges treating AI exposure as more than a single trade, focusing on balance sheet strength, funding visibility, pricing power and returns on incremental capital, and diversifying beyond technology.
UBS moves to overweight the Magnificent Six after being underweight in 1H26, citing attractive valuations and resilient growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient 3Q earnings, robust cloud growth and expanding backlogs point to firm infrastructure demand. The Big 4 hyperscalers and SpaceX are about 80% of 2027 capex, so neocloud stress has limited direct impact.
tension_points.bear_case: Funding is shifting to debt, equity, leases and vendor backstops. CoreWeave's CDS near 1,100bps shows stress at leveraged neoclouds, and UBS sees rising risk of a mid-cycle capex digestion over the next 12 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that demand is no longer keeping pace with supply: weak hyperscaler backlog conversion, slowing AI-lab and cloud revenue growth, falling cloud and GPU hourly pricing, widening neocloud spreads and CDS, and project deferrals or renegotiations.
